name: E-commerce
summary: Online stores selling physical products, mostly on Shopify, in India and the US first, with Amazon as a second surface.
spec: Kevin's ecomOS ingestion spec (ecomos-sources/_INGESTION-SPEC.yaml, version 1, 20 Sep 2026) and generator contract.

constraints.rule: No play is ranked until gross profit per purchase can be computed (MEA). FIN (cash) and OPS (capacity) are preconditions on every play: a plan the brand cannot pay for or staff is not a plan.

house_rules: Brand brain first. Reuse the stored brand file (brand-file.mjs); build and save it only if none exists, never per job. In a job note you never ship: reading level and each persona's own phrases go back to the file; every segment the data ranks, each with its number, stays in the note.

Map every signal to an asset. In your notes, not the deliverable, turn each signal into a named asset where the buyer decides. A past winner gets a relaunch. The best segment gets its own creative, message or ad set. The top return or complaint reason is answered in the bullets and by the button. Every chat or return topic above about 10% gets a fix or a test. A priority the owner names takes a top slot unless the data clearly says otherwise. A signal with no asset is a gap to close.

Look it up before you decide. Before drafting, run `node tools/prepare-job.mjs <brief>` once: it searches the library per data signal and per major decision in the brief and logs each lookup in `context/trace.md`. Read `context/knowledge-brief.md`; ask `node tools/ask-knowledge.mjs` only for a decision it missed. Card ids stay in the trace, never in the deliverable.

Ship what was asked, in full. A copy job ships copy. Add no test budgets, cell plans, measurement sections, rights or contract terms, fallbacks or bolder moves unless the brief asks; at most one line on what to watch. Every customer message is final for every branch that gets it, names the product or answer, and uses only merge fields the brief's tools support, each with a fallback.

Write for a busy owner. Give each decision in two plain lines: what to do, and why, with one number. At most one table per decision, five columns or fewer, no formulas in the body; the working stays in the numbers ledger. Write at the brand's reading level; spell out terms the brief does not use. Stay within the owner's limit and stop when the job is done.

Only the brief's facts run the business. Numbers, dates, windows, age ranges, delays and product specs come from the brief or a logged card. Use relative time (Day 1, Week 2) unless the brief gives dates. Quote product facts and approved claims word for word. When a fact is missing, still deliver every asked-for piece with one assumption line; never drop one to stay safe.

One basis per number. Log each figure with its inputs, period, money basis and source in `context/numbers.json`, and run `node tools/quality/numbers.cjs` before hand-over. Value savings at margin, not order value. Split stock into on hand, held, inbound and sellable before working out cover. One period and one money basis per table. Verdict labels match their numbers: Cut means zero, Trim means lower, Hold means the same, Scale means higher.

Rank in one unit. Size every option in the same unit, tied to the goal the owner named (such as contribution margin or gross profit per month), and show the working. Options sized in mixed units cannot be ranked.
Totals match. Every count, total and target in the summary matches the tables under it, and every target shows its working from the owner's numbers.

Show the after. When you change budgets, prices or offers, forecast gross profit before and after the change, not just the new split. Put the forecast in the numbers ledger, with at most one assumed input, named in the line.

Test at the same time. Compare options in a split run at the same time, with a guardrail metric. Use before and after only when a split is impossible, in matching weeks of the same season, and say so.

Fund each test cell to its read. When the brief asks for a test, run fewer cells, each with enough budget to reach its decision point (cell budget divided by target cost per purchase). If a cell cannot get there, read an earlier metric or merge cells, and say which.
Two reads before a verdict. Judge a channel on at least two reads that agree, such as blended new-customer cost, a post-purchase survey or a holdout, never on tagged orders alone.
Keep the wrong-fit buyer. When a limit causes returns, state it with a number where the buyer decides, and point them to the product that fits.

Each variant earns its own words. Ad and email variants lead with their own angle, in the customers' own phrases where the brief gives them. Proof is a customer's words or one plain claim; a count appears only when the count is the claim, such as a rating with its review total. A stock price or spec line appears in two variants at most.

Publishable means finished. Live copy holds only what the customer reads: no working notes, strategy or monitoring lines, no [X], [link] or TBD, and no private survey quote unless the brief allows it. Check every count and limit with `node tools/quality/copy-check.cjs`. End with no list of things to confirm.

Test where the change lands. Scope each test to the visitors the change touches (device, browser, traffic source or page) and read it at the funnel step the change moves. Keep orders or profit as the guardrail when that step comes earlier.

Spend plans add up. A spend plan adds up to the owner's budget for the period. Any amount held back has a release rule the account can meet within that period, read on store numbers, and is at most 15% of the budget. Fund proven winners from the start where tracking works.

tiers.1: Platform primary source only: Shopify, Meta, Google, Amazon Seller Central or Klaviyo documentation.
tiers.2: Large-sample research or benchmarks: Baymard, academic work, platform benchmark reports, research-grounded books.
tiers.3: A named practitioner showing account-level receipts. Most operator videos.
tiers.4: Opinion with no name or no receipts, or a source with no resolvable date. Hypothesis fuel only.
